name: North Kamrau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog bib holds only surveys/wordlists (Walker 1978 Bomberai Survey; Voorhoeve 1975 checklist; Anceaux 1958); no phonological description found

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. [2020-2024]. North Kamrau. In T. Usher & E. Suter, The Asmat-Muli Languages of Southwestern New Guinea (newguineaworld, Santa Fe Institute; the work Glottolog cites as Usher & Suter 2020).
sources.note: Phonology built from survey wordlists (13 consonants, 5 vowels; /?/ < *k, /h/ < *ɸ; no final consonants). Only stress-related sentence: 'Central vowel [ə] is very common in Walker's vocabularies. It appears to be a destressed allophone of low central /a/.' No statement of where stress falls.

tone.citation_as_reported: Usher, Timothy & Edgar Suter. 2020. The Asmat-Muli Languages of Southwestern New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 38: 148-175.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. n.d. Kamberau Swadesh List (irx). archive.org item rosettaproject_irx_swadesh-1.
sources.note: Wordlist only (multiple dialect forms per gloss, glottal stop written ? or \); no stress marks, no source attribution.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. [2020-2024]. Kamrau Bay (family page) and South Kamrau, same site.
sources.note: Family page: sources list, lexicostatistics (Walker & Hesse 1988), reconstruction; no stress statement. South Kamrau page repeats the 'destressed allophone of /a/' wording; nothing on placement (and it is a different language).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, Bert. 2005. Asmat-Kamoro, Awyu-Dumut and Ok: an enquiry into their linguistic relationships. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds), Papuan Pasts (Pacific Linguistics 572), 145-166.
sources.note: Comparative lexicon; treats Sabakor as one language with a 'Kamrau dialect' (forms mahe'a, ohoroboa cited in notes). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Walker, Roland. 1982. Language use at Namatota: a sociolinguistic profile. In Halim, Carrington & Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics vol. 3 (Pacific Linguistics C-76), 79-94.
sources.note: Mentions Kamberau only as a neighbouring language of the Koiwai; no description.
sources.venue: Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1980. The Asmat languages of Irian Jaya (Pacific Linguistics B-64).
sources.note: Stress and tone section (3.1.2.3) is about Asmat dialects only. Iria-Asienara appears only in comparative notes (noun-class markers -ra / -ka, -?a / -a, -da; pp. 66-67). Nothing on Iria stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum Languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1: Papuan Languages and the New Guinea Linguistic Scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 345-460. Section 2.6.2.2.6.1.1 'Iria and Asienara', pp. 369-370.
sources.note: Only a phoneme inventory 'as far as it could be ascertained from the wordlists' (six stops p t k/? b d g, m n, s h/f (v), r, w y, five or six vowels) and pronouns; 'Language materials are restricted to the lexical data in Anceaux' lists' and 'Further grammatical information is at present not available.' Nothing on stress for Iria (the stress remark on p. 370 concerns Kamoro).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Entry 38 IRIA (Kamrau) and wordlist 38 IRIA (Ac).
sources.note: Checklist entry (850+ speakers, three dialects by village, source Anceaux 1958) and a 40-item wordlist from Anceaux without stress marks. Nothing on stress.
sources.venue: Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page North Kamrau [kamb1302] and hh.bib entries coded [irx].
sources.note: Glottolog lists only a wordlist or less references (Walker 1978; Voorhoeve 1975 x2; Anceaux 1956, 1958) plus Usher & Suter 2020 for subclassification. hh.bib adds Walker & Hesse 1988 'Buruwai' 6-page survey ms. (file, nosharefn), Visser 1989, Ross 1995, Ronsumbre 2020, Rumansara & Kondologit 2018, Naroba 1956 (South Kamrau wordlist). No phonology/grammar of any kind is recorded.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Kamberau language'; Wikidata Q6356317.
sources.note: No phonology section; references only Ethnologue and the newguineaworld page. Wikidata maps irx to kamb1324 (the Kamberau parent node).

sources.note: Secondary mention only: a 60-item vocabulary collected at Wanoma by a fieldworker then working on neighbouring Irarutu; no analysis; at most its phonetic transcription might carry stress marks.
